newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Electrolux earnings slides in gloomy markets.
newsitem.headline: Electrolux earnings slides in gloomy markets.

text.p: Swedish appliance maker Electrolux AB said Tuesday weak markets in all its European businesses and negative currency effects were behind a 13 percent drop in profits for the first nine months of the year.
"The strength of the downturn for white goods (appliances) in Europe surprised us. We had expected a stagnant market," group Chief Executive Leif Johansson told reporters.

The group posted a 2.42 billion crown ($368 million) profit after financial items for the first three quarters of 1996, compared with 2.78 billion ($423 million) reported for the same period a year ago.
Sales for the period fell seven percent to 82.92 billion crowns ($12.6 billion), and Electrolux said currencies had been one of the main contributors to the fall.

"The stronger Swedish crown had an unfavourable effect on sales and income in connection with the translation of financial statements in foreign subsidiaries, and led to a decrease in balance sheet items," the company said.
The stronger Italian lira, an important income currency for the company, was also behind the fall, Ericsson said.
The company also cited a weak performance from the industrial products division, which mainly consists of the Granges engineering unit.
